defects: The handwriting is a typeset script font, not real handwriting. Repeated glyphs and the even, over-wide letter spacing ('kick, live room', 'still no clip') give it away at 100%.
Every tick mark is the same stamped shape with no variation in pressure, angle or ink, so the 'filled in by hand' premise feels machine-made.
The ink is a flat vector blue with no bleed, pressure variation or carbonless-transfer softness, so it sits on top of the paper grain instead of in it.
There is a washed-out, near-white transition frame (pairs row 2, left) that reads as an exposure flash or a cross-dissolve problem rather than a designed beat.
A thin yellow strip of the next layer shows along the bottom edge of the final wide frame (pairs row 3, right), which is an edge or compositing slip.
The 'Te…' of 'Tern' writes on letter by letter at a constant rate with no stroke timing, so there is no pen acceleration or lift.
Shots run to 8.8 s and the median is 5 s. Six of the 29 seconds look almost the same as the second before, so slow camera drifts across a static sheet become dead air.
The circles around the good takes are the best-drawn element, but they overlap the neighbouring rows and clip the text ('still no c…') in a way that looks accidental rather than urgent.
gaps: Motion is almost entirely slow camera push and pan over a flat sheet, plus linear write-ons. Top work would choreograph the pen as a character (pressure, speed changes, lifts, crossings-out with real attack) and cut hard on the moments that matter: the strikethrough, the 'Tern' circle, '30 hrs, one roll'. Shots should be around 2 s, and the build should come from editing rhythm, not from drifting.

Sound: the spectrogram shows a dense, full-band, produced bed with a deliberate drop around 6.5–7.5 s, which is good. After that it is a steady wall of evenly spaced transients with almost no dynamic shape. Nothing in it is specific to the subject, such as pen scratch, paper handling, or the field sounds the sheet names (rain, thunder, a door slamming), so a concept about recording sound never lets you hear what was recorded.

Finish: the idea of a pink carbonless sound report is strong and the palette is restrained. But the fake script font, the cloned ticks and the flat vector ink undercut the material honesty the concept depends on. Real scanned handwriting, ink that absorbs into the paper, the carbon-copy offset and lighting with falloff would lift it from template to studio work.
